questions.question: A life policy has predetermined level premium $P$, unit premium-stream PV $Y$ with $0<E[Y]<\infty$, and dependent random benefit and expense PVs $Z,H$. All expectations are finite, $E[H]>0$, and expenses do not depend on $P$. Does their dependence require changing the gross equivalence balance?
options: Yes; add a covariance correction to expected total cost.
No; expected total cost remains the sum of the two expectations.
Yes; replace the cost sum by the expected benefit-expense product.
No; dependent expenses may be omitted from expected total cost.

questions.question: For one life-insurance contract let $b>0$ be benefit APV, $h>0$ expense APV independent of the level premium and $a>0$ unit premium-stream APV. The net and gross premiums use the same valuation basis. Which pair gives them respectively?
A premium has been chosen so that expected discounted premium income equals expected discounted benefits and expenses at issue. What does this imply about one insured policy?
options: Its realised discounted income and cost may differ.
Its realised discounted income must equal its cost.
Its undiscounted income must equal its undiscounted cost.
Its realised income must exceed its cost on every lifetime.

questions.question: An insurer quotes a level premium by dividing expected discounted costs by the APV of a unit premium stream. Which practice gives a coherent equivalence calculation for every specified mortality and interest basis, including contingent premium receipts?
options: Use the intended basis for benefits and zero interest for premiums.
Use unconditional benefit costs but condition premiums on surviving every payment date.
Value both cash-flow sides on the same mortality and interest basis.
Use the total scheduled premium count without survival weights.

questions.question: A net whole-life premium is paid annually in advance while alive. Let $K\ge0$ be integer curtate future lifetime and $v>0$ the annual discount factor. Which formula is the unit premium-stream PV for every admissible $K,v$, before expectation is taken?
A life policy has benefit APV 54 and unit annual premium-stream APV 12 on its pricing basis. Expenses are omitted. What level annual premium satisfies net equivalence?

On the same basis, a life policy has unit annual premium-stream APV 8. Adding premium-independent expenses with APV 6 leaves benefits and premium dates unchanged. By how much must its gross annual premium exceed its net premium?

A policy has benefit APV 30, fixed expense APV 5 and unit annual premium-stream APV 10. A revision doubles every benefit amount but leaves expenses and premium dates unchanged. What gross annual premium does equivalence require after revision?

A policy has benefit APV 171 and no expenses. Level premiums $P$ are paid at times 0, 1 and 2 only if alive, with survival probabilities 1, 0.8 and 0.6 respectively. The annual discount factor is $v=0.9$. What is the required annual premium?

A life policy has benefit APV 36 and unit annual premium-stream APV 9. Each premium actually received incurs an expense equal to 20% of that receipt; no other expenses apply. What level annual premium satisfies gross equivalence?

Two net life policies have the same positive benefit APV and the same unit premium amounts at shared dates. The second permits fewer premium-payment dates; the removed dates have positive survival probability. Discount factors are positive and both unit-stream APVs are finite and positive. How do their level premiums compare?
options: The shorter premium stream requires a smaller level premium.
The premiums agree because the death cover is unchanged.
The shorter premium stream requires a smaller death benefit.
The shorter premium stream requires a larger level premium.

questions.question: For a net life policy let $Z\ge0$ be benefit PV and $Y>0$ unit premium-stream PV, with finite expectations. The level premium $P$ is predetermined. Which equivalence identity is valid for every admissible joint law of $Z,Y$?

A gross life-policy price has unit premium-stream APV $a>0$ and benefit APV $b>0$. Expense APV is $h(P)$, a specified function of the level premium $P$. A proposed method evaluates $h$ at the net premium $b/a$ and then sets $P=[b+h(b/a)]/a$. What condition must still be checked for that proposed price to satisfy gross equivalence?

For unit annual-settlement whole-life insurance, let benefit APV be $A=0.4$. Annual premiums are paid in advance while alive, and the unit annuity-due APV $a$ satisfies $A+d a=1$, where the discount rate is $d=0.05$. With no expenses, what is the annual premium?

A life policy has benefit APV 24 and unit annual premium-stream APV 6. At issue it incurs a single expense equal to half of the level annual premium $P$, independent of how many later premiums are received. No other expenses apply. What is its gross annual premium?

A life policy has benefit APV 80 and unit annual premium-stream APV 10. Expenses are a fixed amount 4 at issue and 10% of each premium actually received. What level annual premium $P$ satisfies gross equivalence?

For a general level-premium arrangement, let $Y\ge0$ be unit premium-stream present value with $E[Y]=0$. Let $c\ge0$ be finite expected discounted benefits plus premium-independent expenses. Under the equation $P E[Y]=c$, which statement correctly separates the cases?
options: If $c>0$, the premium is $c$; if $c=0$, only zero solves it.
If $c>0$, no finite premium solves it; if $c=0$, every finite premium solves it.
If $c>0$, only zero solves it; if $c=0$, no finite premium solves it.
If $c>0$, no finite premium solves it; if $c=0$, only zero solves it.

questions.question: A deterministic insurance arrangement collects two level premiums $P$ at times 0 and 1 and pays benefit $2P$ at time 2, with no expenses. The annual discount factor is $0<v<1$ and $P>0$. Its total undiscounted receipts and benefit agree. Does it satisfy discounted equivalence?
options: Yes: equality of the two undiscounted totals is sufficient.
Yes: discounting both totals at time 2 preserves the original equality.

questions.question: A life-policy illustration has unit premium-stream APV 8 and benefit APV 12. Its single issue expense has amount $P^2$ when the level premium is $P\ge0$. Which set contains all non-negative premiums satisfying gross equivalence?

A policy has expected benefit cost 15 and unit premium-stream APV 3. A single issue expense has amount $4P$, where $P\ge0$ is the level premium; there are no other expenses. What happens when gross equivalence is imposed?
options: The premium is $15/7$, using both income and expense coefficients.
The premium is $15$, using the absolute coefficient difference.
The premium is $5$, using the benefit and premium-stream APVs.
The equation gives $P=-15$, so no non-negative premium satisfies it.
